title: From idea to almost launch: one year building Vaelix with AI
author: NicoBacc
selftext:
I've been working on this for almost a year now, and we're finally getting pretty close to releasing it, so I thought this was probably the right place to share some of the process.

I'm a developer and I've been building apps and websites for around 10 years. Games were never really my main field, although years ago I did build an online 3D racing game in Unity. It actually worked and had multiplayer, but eventually I shut it down because the playerbase wasn't really there anymore.

Vaelix started as another attempt at making a game, but this time the situation was a bit different. We are a small team of 4 developers and a tester, but we don't have a dedicated game designer / graphic designer in the team. That's probably the area where AI made the biggest difference for us. Without it, I honestly don't think we could have taken the game this far with the team we have.

We used ChatGPT a lot at the beginning to brainstorm the game itself, challenge some of the ideas, define the mechanics and basically turn everything into a development plan and a long list of tasks. From there most of the first implementation was done through OpenCode, mainly using DeepSeek V4.1 and GLM 5.3. More recently we've been using Claude quite a lot for the boring but important part: going through the code, finding edge cases, fixing bugs, questioning some of our decisions and generally polishing things.

AI was also a huge help for the part we were missing completely in the team. Most of the assets, characters, UI elements and audio started from AI-generated material and then went through quite a bit of iteration before actually ending up in the game.

The game itself is called **Vaelix**. It's a fast 3v3 tactical game where both players plan their actions at the same time instead of taking traditional turns. Once both sides are ready, everything resolves together, so a big part of the game is trying to predict what the other player is going to do rather than just reacting to it.

Positioning is probably the most important part. Different heroes can move enemies around, teleport, create dangerous areas, protect teammates, bring someone back to a previous position and so on, so even fairly simple actions can interact in ways that we didn't expect when we first designed them. There's also a Collapse mechanic that progressively closes the arena, mostly because during testing we quickly discovered that giving players the option to play defensively forever was... not a great idea 😅

Technically the game is built in **Flutter + Firebase**. Flutter probably wouldn't have been my first answer a few years ago if someone asked me what to use for a multiplayer tactical game, but since it's the ecosystem we already know very well we decided to try it, and so far I'm actually really happy with the result.

We're currently in the final testing/polishing phase, doing lots of matches, fixing weird interactions and finishing the last pieces before launch. The current plan is to release in **November**.

The video is a look at where the game is right now. Still a few things to improve, but after staring at it every day for so long it's honestly nice to finally show it to people outside the team.

I'd be really interested in feedback, especially from people here who have gone through the same process of building a game with AI as part of the workflow.

If anyone wants to follow the project or join the waitlist, we just put the website online:

[**https://vaelix.app**](https://vaelix.app)
